name: solvent-front
title: Solvent Front
description: A part-of-whole breakdown drawn as paper chromatography: one opaque spot at a strip's baseline resolves, as a solvent front climbs, into stacked bands that each halt at a height proportional to their share of the total.
useWhen: a single total the user just incurred needs to resolve into its shares as one continuous separation — an LLM bill into model/input/output/cache, a bundle into dependency sizes — where the un-split whole belongs on screen for a beat before it divides. Pick chart-funnel-stage-drop instead when the values are sequential stages that arrive and drop off one after another rather than static shares of one total, and litmus-wick when the fact worth showing is a threshold pass/fail on a single value, not a multi-way breakdown.
instruction: SolventFront<total? bands? title? unit? decimals? className?> renders a tall thin 1px --border strip on --background and, on mount, replays the moment a total resolves into its components as literal paper chromatography — never a bar or pie redrawing itself. Every band shares one baseline `top` at rest, so before anything moves they render as one solid, 1px-blurred bar: that overlap IS the brief's 'single opaque spot', with no separate blob element required. After a fixed HOLD (500ms, the un-separated whole sitting still and legible before it splits), a single boolean flip transitions three things at once, purely via CSS `top` transitions (no rAF drives position, so nothing fights layout): the solvent-front line and the wet-tint backdrop behind it both ease from the baseline to the strip's top over 1600ms on ease-out-expo (cubic-bezier(0.16,1,0.3,1), this registry's existing convention for that curve), while every band eases from the same baseline to its own target height — `stripHeight * (1 - share)` — on a bouncier spring curve (cubic-bezier(0.34,1.56,0.64,1)). Because every band shares one duration but travels a distance set by its own share of the total (its Rf), a band with a small share travels a short distance and visibly settles, spring-soft, well before the front — which always travels the full strip height — finishes climbing past it: the front literally outruns it. The wet region is a flat `color-mix(in srgb, var(--foreground) 2%, var(--background))` fill, the only fill on the strip beyond the bands themselves; no gradients anywhere. Each band's edges are feathered by a `::before` pseudo-element on a separate absolutely-positioned fill span (never on the button itself), carrying `filter: blur(1px)`, so the blur softens the visible edge without touching the real (crisp) hit target underneath. Every band is a real, always-focusable `<button>` (DOM order = descending value, so Tab visits them in value order with no roving-tabindex bookkeeping needed) whose accessible name already carries its final value and share percentage, and which is additionally `aria-describedby` its own `<dd>` in a real, visible `<dl>` legend rendered right below the strip — so the exact figures exist as plain text from the very first paint, independent of whether the entrance animation has finished. Hovering or focusing a band projects its retention height onto a tick-marked edge ruler to the strip's left: a dashed `--ns-accent` line runs from the ruler to the band's settled height, with a small dot and its share percentage in `--ns-accent` (var(--ns-accent) is used nowhere else — resting ink is pure `--foreground` bands, `--ns-muted` ruler ticks and secondary labels). A second, `aria-hidden` copy of each band's value sits beside the strip in Geist Mono and ticks upward from 0 to its final figure in step with the shared reveal progress (one small rAF loop, decimals only, driving text content, never layout), fading in as the band leaves the baseline. `prefers-reduced-motion` (read live via `matchMedia`, listened for changes) skips the hold and every transition/tick entirely and paints the fully separated final state — bands at their settled heights, labels at full value — on the very first frame. Props: `total` (defaults to the sum of `bands`), `bands` (`{id,label,value}[]`, defaults to a four-way LLM bill: output/input/cache-write/cache-read tokens), `title`, `unit` (value prefix, default "$"), `decimals` (default 2), `className`. Zero dependencies.
